result.note: Stage 2c: @on_* handler bodies gain a best-effort parsed AST (GameEventBlockNode.parsed_body) produced by a speculative parse over the TOKEN STREAM, and @unknown enforcement now reaches inside them. The raw `body` capture is unchanged and still authoritative; the speculative parse always restores the cursor, so a body that no statement grammar accepts is DECLINED (parsed_body: None) rather than rejected -- the tolerance contract is preserved. Parsing from tokens rather than re-lexing `body` is required, not stylistic: the raw text is lossy (string quotes stripped, escapes decoded, and `??` flattened to `? ?` because `?` lexes single-char), so the null-coalescing guard only survives via the token path. No wasm_bindgen export was added or removed; JS glue and .d.ts are byte-identical and the 8 exports are unchanged. MEASURED COVERAGE across the corpus (2308 .hsplus scanned, 2241 files containing handlers): 5013 handler bodies, 4062 parsed and therefore analyzed (81.0%), 951 declined and therefore UNANALYZED (19.0%) -- unanalyzed is deliberately distinct from analyzed-and-clean, and that 19% is the honest remaining gap, not a rounding error. Verified against the declared authority corpus via the differential (which calls validate_detailed, so it exercises the semantic check as well as the parser): 2303 files, Rust pass rate 2256/2303 (97.96%), 0 files regressed vs the 2026-07-17 baseline -- byte-for-byte identical figures to before the change, in 11.9s, so the speculative parse is behavior-neutral and cheap. cargo test -p holoscript-wasm 222 passed (6 new); cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean. Source changes are committed with this receipt, so the working-tree suffix resolves to that commit.
